column2: An AWS identity with permissions that can be assumed by trusted users, applications, or AWS services. It provides temporary credentials rather than long-term credentials.

column1: Which IAM security tool reports the credential status of all IAM users in an AWS account?
column2: IAM Credentials Report. It is an account-level report covering IAM users and the status of their passwords, access keys, and MFA credentials.

column1: Do IAM users access AWS using the root account’s credentials?
column2: No. IAM users use their own console credentials or access keys. Root credentials should not be shared or used for routine work.
A JSON document defining permissions for AWS actions and resources. Policies can be associated with IAM users, groups, roles, and some AWS resources.

column1: Can an IAM user group contain another IAM user group?
column2: No. IAM user groups cannot be nested. A group can contain IAM users, and a user can belong to multiple groups.

column1: Which element belongs to the overall IAM policy rather than an individual policy statement?
column2: Version. A statement can contain elements such as Sid, Effect, Action, Resource, Condition, and sometimes Principal.
